abstract: Phage lytic proteins are promising antibacterial and biotechnological candidates, yet uncertain annotations, modular architectures, and class imbalance complicate sequence-based classification. We developed PhageLysClass, an evidence-aware framework for recognizing lytic proteins and distinguishing Endolysins, Depolymerases, and virion-associated lytic enzymes. From 442,329 unique phage sequences, including 11,867 evidence-supported positives, we defined distinct candidate non-target, unlabeled, and challenge populations. Seven supervised and two positive-unlabeled tasks were evaluated across factorial redundancy and train-test homology conditions, yielding 2,240 and 768 experiments, respectively. Redundancy reduction influenced generalization more strongly than homology separation, with non-additive interactions between them. ESM2-T30 consistently outperformed alternative representations and supported a hierarchical classifier achieving approximately 0.89 MCC under strict R30/S30 conditions in the selected, pre-refitting benchmark. Applied without retraining to 77,897 sequences across three collections, PhageLysClass combined predictions with physicochemical and geometric contextualization, highlighting Depolymerase-like candidates among structurally ambiguous proteins while distinguishing reference-supported assignments from extrapolation.
